SOURCE DEPTH / VISIBLE LIMITATIONS

Useful preparation. Honest evidence.

The release connects the complete North American backlog to the site. Only individually source-checked records are called guides.

Source-checked guides

38

Full source-page text supports named claims. Not field-tested or independently expert-reviewed.

Source-linked briefs

279

Retained starting points. Many are supported only by inspected search excerpts and require deeper review.

Preparation frameworks

479

Production briefs with local questions and equipment decisions. No local evidence has been verified yet.

What changed in this release.

All 507 U.S., Canadian and Mexican production entries now have a canonical trip page, a state/province collection and a connected planner. Existing matches were retained; one overlapping Great Bear Lake pair was merged. The resulting global count is 796—not 816.

Ten local guides received source-page research in this release: eight Southeast guides and two Texas guides. These pages cite their specific claims. Other imports remain preparation frameworks, with candidate species and access clearly unverified.

Search eligibility is separate from browsing. Unfinished and excerpt-only trip pages are excluded from the production sitemap and carry noindex. A real production origin must still be configured before any page is indexable.

Source register.

Some records refer to the same webpage in different editions. The 217 count is a source-record count, not a unique-URL count or a count of freshly reviewed pages.

Coverage is not completeness.

Profiles are fishing experiences, not necessarily unique lakes or rivers. Multiple methods can share a location; shared waters can have different departure contexts. Region names are editorial groupings. Missing countries, species or months remain gaps—not claims that fishing is absent.
